EX-PARTE JUDGMENT 1.
Vide this judgment, the present suit for recovery of Rs. 4,20,872.90p shall be disposed of.
Submissions have been heard.
File has been perused.
2. Summons of the suit were issued to the defendant.
Summons could not be served upon the defendant through ordinary modes.
Summons were served upon the defendant through email on 30.10.2023.
None appeared on behalf of the defendant.
No written statement was filed on behalf of defendant.

The right of the defendant to file written statement was forfeited and defendant was proceeded against ex-parte vide order dated 28.03.2024.
3.
Issues were thus not required to be framed.
The plaintiff was called upon to lead ex-parte evidence.
The plaintiff examined Sh. Manoj CS (Comm) 350/23 Date of Judgment : 20.09.2025 rv Kumar as PW1.

sentences.text:
The Plaintiff is a juristic entity having its Head Office at Bank Of Baroda vs Anuradha on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83272389/
3 Mandavi, Baroda, and is carrying on the business of banking through its various branches all over India, including one branch at Khureji Khas, Delhi- 110092.The plaint has been signed and verified by Mr. Vipin Kumar, who is stated to be duly authorized to do so.
5.
The defendant approached the plaintiff's bank on 03.11.2021 for grant of a loan facility under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) for business of manufacturing of vegetable oil and processing units.

After satisfying itself, the CS (Comm) 350/23 Date of Judgment : 20.09.2025 rv plaintiff bank sanctioned a Working Capital Cash Credit Facility of Rs. 4,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakh only) to the defendant under PMMY scheme vide loan account no. 76640500000296.
6.

It is stated that in order to secure the repayment of the said facility, defendant had signed and executed various documents such as Demand Promissory Note, Letter of Sole Proprietorship, Letter of Continuing Security, Draft Undertaking, Declaration cum Undertaking cum Authority and Composite Hyphothecation Agreement.
Defendant accepted the terms and conditions for repayment the loan.
The rate of the interest was agreed to be paid on floating basis i.e. 7.45% per annum with monthly rests.
The defendant further agreed to pay penal interest @ 2% p.a. in case of default in payment.
The loan was to be repaid in 12 months subject to annual review by the plaintiff.
7. The defendant did not comply with the terms and conditions.
The defendant defaulted in making payments.
Consequently, the said loan account became highly irregular in terms of non-payment.
Despite various reminders/letters/notices sent to the defendant for repayment of the dues but in vain.
Accordingly, plaintiff issued a demand notice dated 10.05.2023 upon the defendant thereby recalling the loan agreement.
The loan account of the defendant was classified as NPA on 04.04.2023 as per the guidelines of Reserve Bank of India.
The defendant has paid last payment of Rs.1,000/- on 03.03.2023.
The plaintiff bank also approached East District Legal Authority for pre- litigation mediation.

A non starter report was issued by the authority on CS (Comm) 350/23 Date of Judgment : 20.09.2025 rv 15.07.2023.
8.

The plaintiff, therefore, seeks a decree of amount Rs.4,20,872.90 (Rupees Four Lakhs Twenty Thousand Eight Hundred Seventy Two and Ninety Paise Only) alongwith pendente-lite and future interest at the rate 10.20% per annum, also 2.00% penal interest from the date of filing of suit till realization alongwith cost of the suit.
Contentions of the plaintiff 9.
The Ld. counsel for the plaintiff reiterated the averments contained in the plaint.
He submitted that the defendant did not clear the outstanding dues.
Therefore, defendant was liable to pay the outstanding dues.
He prayed for interest to be awarded at the rate sought as well as for costs of the suit to be awarded to the plaintiff.
Observation of the Court 10.
The defendant was proceeded against ex-parte.
Defendant did not file any written statement nor led any evidence on her behalf.
The plaintiff's witness was not even cross-examined on her behalf.

Bank Of Baroda vs Anuradha on 20 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83272389/
4
The testimony of PW1 thus remains unrebutted.
There is nothing on record to lead the court to disbelieve such unrebutted testimony 11.
The cash credit facility was availed by the defendant on 08.11.2021.
CS (Comm) 350/23 Date of Judgment : 20.09.2025 rv
Defendant made some payments, the last of which was made on 03.03.2023.
Statement of account is maintained by the plaintiff.
Despite availing the said facility, the defendant failed to make payment, thereby breaching her contractual obligations.
This conduct clearly evidences a willful default and renders the defendant liable for both the principal amount and interest.
The present suit filed on 13.09.2023, falls well within the statutory limitation period of three years and is therefore legally maintainable.
This court has jurisdiction to entertain and try the suit as the loan facility was availed by the defendant and was to be repaid within the jurisdiction of this court.
The plaintiff had also complied with the mandate of Section 12A of The Commercial Courts Act.
12. Having not repaid the amount availed and enjoyed by the defendant, the defendant is liable to pay the amount claimed by the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has sought interest @ 10.20% p.a and penal interest @ 2.00% per annum.
Such rate of interest is found to be excessive.
Interests of justice would be served by granting pendente lite and future interest @ 8% per annum.

13. In the light of the above discussions, the suit of the plaintiff is decreed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant for the amount of Rs.4,20,872.90 (Rupees Four Lakhs Twenty Thousand Eight Hundred Seventy Two and Ninety Paise Only) with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of filing of the suit (i.e. 13.09.2023) till realization of the amount.
Costs of the suit are also awarded to the plaintiff.
14. Decree sheet be accordingly drawn.
Copy of judgment be supplied to the CS (Comm) 350/23 Date of Judgment : 20.09.2025 rv Ld.
Counsel for the parties in terms of Order XX Rule 1 CPC, as amended by the Commercial Courts Act, 2015.
15. File be consigned to record room thereafter.
